summary: L-4 cliffside lookout in Gifford Pinchot National Forest, staffed into the mid-2000s and now off-site for restoration of the cabin.

facts.status_note: Cabin removed from the tower base for off-site restoration (reported 2021-2024); not currently rentable.

access.note: Reached by a ~1.6 mile trail off FS Road 52; site is historic and not rented.

visit.trail_note: ~1.6 mile hike, usually snow-free by early July; signage sparse past the gravel road turnoff.

events.note: NHLR gives 1929; Fire Lookout Museum gives 1930 for the L-4 cab.
Staffed the same year it was built, per NHLR.
Certificate presented June 2001 to District Ranger Harry Cody and observer Bud Panco.
Fire Lookout Museum says staffed into the mid-2000s; exact last year not given.
Cab removed from site for off-site restoration per Fire Lookout Museum.
NHLR notes the cabin still undergoing off-site restoration as of 2024; not yet confirmed returned to the tower.

evidence.supports: Perched on a 1200' cliff, L-4 cab built 1929, staffed same year, NHLR certificate June 2001 to Cody and Panco.
evidence.quote: The 14' x 14' gable roof L-4 ground house with catwalk was built in 1929 and staffed the same year. It is perched on the edge of a 1200' sheer cliff.

evidence.supports: Built 1930, staffed into the mid-2000s, cab removed 2021 for off-site restoration.
evidence.quote: Built in 1930, this gable-roofed L-4 cab atop a 1/2 story base was staffed during the summer in to the mid-2000's. In 2021, the cab was removed for off-site restoration.

evidence.supports: 2017 site visit found broken/boarded windows, graffiti, droppings, firefinder still in place, ceiling reinforcements added.
evidence.quote: Mouse droppings abound. Firefinder still in place. A bunch of trash in the attic. I believe every window had panes missing, and a number were boarded over.

evidence.supports: 2024 status: platform shown during off-site restoration of cabin.
evidence.quote: Platform during off-site restoration of cabin in 2024 - courtesy of Todd Stewart

evidence.supports: Trail is ~1.6 miles, usually snow-free by July 1, signage sparse.
evidence.quote: The historic site is carefully maintained by the Forest Service and is reached by a 1.6 mile trail which is usually free of snow by July 1.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1929 (built and staffed same year); Fire Lookout Museum gives 1930. Both are kept in the story as a disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Did not find a source confirming the current (2026) status of the restoration — last confirmed info is the NHLR's 2024 note that the cabin was still off-site. Worth a follow-up check with the Gifford Pinchot NF or NHLR for an update before calling it 'restored' outright.
